summary: The design is implementable, but several choices need tightening before coding: voice successor IDs are not present in the checked-in catalogues, Argon changes cache behavior, and broad source scanning conflicts with stated non-goals. The highest risks are public enum/API breakage, legacy computer-use routing, inconsistent fallback policy, and explicit deployment overrides that remain untouched.

suggestions.title: Verify voice replacements against the live API
suggestions.rationale: The repository contains 2.5 native-audio/TTS defaults and only 3.1 TTS/live successors; neither `gemini-3.8-live` nor `gemini-3.8-flash-tts` exists in the checked-in catalogues. `GeminiLiveClient` consumes `GoogleVoiceModel.DEFAULT`, while speech generation directly defaults to the retired enum member. Make live model discovery plus feature-specific connect/generate checks a blocking gate before deleting the old IDs, with direct tests for both defaults.

suggestions.title: Treat Argon cache loss as an explicit product contract
suggestions.rationale: The cache helper calls `caches.create` for any model and catches every exception, leaving the request unchanged. Existing tests prove generic fail-open behavior with a 2.5 string, but not the new Argon defaults. Add an Argon-specific path test asserting system instructions survive, and decide whether to expose a cache-skipped signal or keep cache-dependent components on flash.

suggestions.title: Resolve the `gemini-flash-latest` versus `gemini-3.8-flash` fallback policy
suggestions.rationale: `GoogleGenAIClient._default_model` is currently `gemini-flash-latest`, while the proposed mapping names `gemini-3.8-flash` and suggests mixing `self._default_model` with explicit 3.8 fallbacks. That would make ask, streaming, batch, question, and analysis paths choose different models. Define one policy and test every fallback path before replacing the seven client literals.

suggestions.title: Separate catalogue retirement from legacy computer-use routing
suggestions.rationale: The client explicitly documents that legacy computer-use identifiers remain enabled, `_is_computer_use_model` still recognizes the 2.5 computer-use prefix, and tests assert its legacy vocabulary. Removing that prefix is a behavioral compatibility break, not merely enum cleanup. Either retain string routing while removing catalogue publication, or define and test an explicit unsupported-model transition.

suggestions.title: Use exact pricing coverage for Argon
suggestions.rationale: `CostCalculator` performs `provider_pricing.get(model)` with no prefix matching. `gemini-3.8-flash` already has a dated pricing row; the missing operational row is `gemini-4-argon`, which currently returns an unpriced result. Add externally verified Argon rates and tests for both `cost_usd` and `revision_for` using provider `gemini`.

suggestions.title: Make the public enum deletion policy explicit
suggestions.rationale: `GoogleModel` is exported from the Google client package, used by `LLMFactory`, and iterated by the models HTTP handler. Deleting members breaks Python imports and `GoogleModel(old_id)` parsing in addition to changing `/models`. If pure deletion is required, document the breaking contract and add negative tests; otherwise separate active publication from legacy parsing.

suggestions.title: Make the retirement guard token-aware and consistent with non-goals
suggestions.rationale: A broad `gemini-2.5-flash` textual scan would also match intentionally retained `flash-lite` and `flash-image` values, while `clients/base.py` still contains 2.5 documentation despite being declared untouched. Scan exact model tokens in executable call sites or maintain a narrow, reviewed exclusion list rather than asserting that no substring survives under all `src`.

suggestions.title: Validate hand-maintained UI models against the backend catalogue
suggestions.rationale: The UI lists `gemini-3-pro-preview`, which is not a current enum value, and `gemini-3-flash-preview`, which is represented in the backend as a computer-use model. Because the UI list is independent of `/models`, updating only the 2.5 entries can leave invalid choices. Add a consistency test or derive enabled choices from the backend catalogue.

suggestions.title: Add an operational migration contract for explicit overrides
suggestions.rationale: `resolve_component_llm` accepts arbitrary model strings, and `conf.py` reads `LLM_MODEL` directly. Existing environment variables, persisted bot configurations, and `DEFAULT_LLM` therefore remain able to select retired IDs even after builtins change; Google auto-routing can silently alter cost and behavior. Document the migration and test that explicit overrides are intentionally preserved rather than mistaken for migrated defaults.

suggestions.title: Keep the SDK floor bump independently gate-verifiable
suggestions.rationale: Both declared Google SDK constraints are `>=2.31.0` and the lock resolves 2.31.0, while the client exercises caches, computer-use, live sessions, and generation APIs. Verify the exact candidate in an isolated environment against those surfaces and lock only that dependency, ideally in a separate commit or independently diagnosable task from enum deletion.

suggestions.title: Resolve the pre-existing `google:gemini-3-flash` drift explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `WebSearchAgent` defaults to `google:gemini-3-flash`, but the catalogue maps `GEMINI_3_FLASH` to `gemini-3.5-flash` and has no `gemini-3-flash` member except the computer-use preview entry. Correct this while the model sweep is open, or mark it as a tested non-goal so the retirement does not preserve an invalid adjacent default.
